Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 13807 of 2022
Applicant :- Pujjan
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt., Lko. And 3 Others

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashish Raman Mishra,Aradhana Chaturvedi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Mohd. Faiz Alam Khan,J.
As per the report of the office the notice was sent to the opposite party no.2 and the same has been personally served.
However, no one is present for the opposite party no.2/complainant/informant.
Heard Shri Ashish Raman Mishra, learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

This bail application has been moved by the accused/applicant- Pujjan for grant of bail, in Case Crime No. 454 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station Ramgaon, District Bahraich, during trial.
Learned counsel for the accused-applicant while pressing the bail application submits that it is a case of false implication.

The F.I.R. of the instant case was lodged by the father of the prosecutrix on 02.09.2022 at Police Station Ramgaon, District Bahraich alleging therein that the accused persons named therein had enticed away the prosecutrix aged about 15 years.

However, on being recovered,
the statement of the prosecutrix was recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., wherein she stated her age to be of 19 years and also that on 29.08.2022 at about 4:00 pm.

she had called the accused at the Pujjan vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home ... on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5057467/
1 bus station of Bahraich and from there they had gone to Lucknow and thereafter to Mumbai where they solemnized marriage.
It is further submitted that in the statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix has stated her age to be of 19 years and emphasized that on 29.08.2022 at about 4:00 pm.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: she herself called the accused to the bus stand of Bahraich and they had gone to Mumbai and solemnized marriage and when they came to know that the family members of the prosecutrix have lodged an F.I.R., they returned back.

Highlighting the above statements of the prosecutrix, it is vehemently submitted that the prosecutrix was a consenting party and she had herself called the accused to the bus stand of Bahraich and it was she who has persuaded the applicant to flee with her.

While drawing the attention of this Court towards paragraph nos. 13, 14 and 15 of the bail application, it is further submitted that the prosecutrix was earlier married against her will,
however, her in-laws did not take her and she, at the date and time of the incident was major, as she in her statements recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. had stated her age to be of 19 years and having regard to her admission pertaining to her age the educational certificate collected by the investigating officer would not be of any consequence, as in her 'Aadhar Card' also, the date of birth of the prosecutrix has been shown as 01.01.2003.
It is next submitted that applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 10.09.2022 and he is not having any criminal history.
Charge sheet in this case has already been filed and there is no apprehension that after being released on bail he may flee from the course of law or may otherwise misuse the liberty.
Learned A.G.A., however, opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on the ground that the applicant has committed an heinous offence and, therefore, he is not entitled to be released on bail.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, it is evident that the age of the prosecutrix has been shown as 15 years in the first information report, however, in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. she stated her age to be of 19 years while as per her educational credentials her date of birth is shown as 15.05.2007, while in the 'Aadhar Card' a copy of which has been placed on record as Annexure No.7, her date of birth is shown as 01.01.2003 and it is in the background of these documents, it is vehemently submitted that when as per her own admission the age of the prosecutrix is about 19 years, the same should be taken as genuine.

The prosecutrix in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. had clearly stated that it was she (prosecutrix), who had persuaded the applicant to come at Bus Station, Bahraich and from there they had gone to Lucknow and, thereafter, to Mumbai where they have solemnized marriage and were living as husband and wife and getting information about the proceedings of the instant case they had returned back.
Applicant is languishing in jail in this case since 10.09.2022 without any criminal antecedents.
Charge sheet in this case has also been filed.
The guilt of the applicant is to be determined during the course of trial and the presence of the applicant may be secured before the trial court by placing adequate conditions.

sentences.text: Keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the considered view that applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is thus allowed.

Let the accused/applicant- Pujjan involved in above-mentioned case, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence by intimidating/pressurizing the witnesses, during the investigation or trial.
(ii) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the Court concerned before the bonds are accepted.
Observations made herein-above by this court are only for the purpose of disposal of this bail application and shall not be construed as an expression on the merits of the case.
